headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible between Flowise and Roo Code.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and uploaded files, while Roo Code reads/writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP. A shared filesystem bridge makes attacker-controlled content from one agent plausibly reach the other as trusted input. This is not proven by docs as a default direct channel, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Flowise writes attacker-controlled content into a shared workspace or datastore that Roo Code later reads
IF Roo Code ingests file contents or MCP outputs as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces or volumes
Disable MCP servers for Roo Code during shared runs
Add a manual review step before Roo Code consumes Flowise-generated files
Use read-only mounts for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model provider keys. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so a shared workspace can expose sensitive material across agents. The profiles do not show a guaranteed leak, but the default overlap is enough for medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or datastore
IF either agent writes secrets or chatflow inputs to files that the other can read
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to a configured model API
mitigations: Keep secrets in separate credential stores per agent
Use distinct directories for Flowise and Roo Code
Rotate any exposed API keys after shared runs
Restrict outbound network access for one agent during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, read files, and use broad network egress; Roo Code also modifies git state and runs shell commands, while Flowise writes server-side files in a shared datastore model. That creates a direct conflict over mutable resources, and the Roo Code filesystem-sharing model makes collisions likely without locks. High is warranted because git or workspace corruption can be irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Roo Code performs git writes while Flowise writes generated artifacts into the same tree
IF no external locking or serialization is configured
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or directories
Pause one agent while the other performs writes
Avoid git operations in Roo Code during shared sessions
Use file locks or a single-writer queue
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and Roo Code is an action-taking coding agent with terminal approval and browser/tool use. If Roo Code treats Flowise output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes, shell actions, or browser-driven actions. The interaction is plausible by default and the blast radius can be substantial.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes Flowise-generated text, plans, or tool outputs without verification
IF Flowise is used to generate facts or instructions that Roo Code then executes
IF approval prompts are accepted without independent review
mitigations: Require Roo Code to verify Flowise outputs against source files
Insert a human review step before any terminal or git action
Limit Flowise to advisory outputs only
Disable automatic execution of generated commands
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent messages

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets on a server datastore, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots in a VS Code workspace. Their storage and retention behaviors are different and not documented as aligned, so the same data class can be retained or logged differently across the pair. The profiles do not show a residency breach, but policy mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF the same regulated data is processed by both agents
IF one agent retains workspace or datastore artifacts longer than the other
IF organizational policy requires uniform deletion or export handling
mitigations: Document retention rules for each agent
Avoid sending regulated data to both agents
Delete shared artifacts immediately after use
Keep separate audit logs per agent
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the deployment
